    StartersCarnival corn dogsCocktail franks in a cornmeal buttermilk batter, friedHow to make it24 cocktail franks24 skewers100g fine cornmeal100g plain flour1 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp yellow mustard4 tbsp tomato sauceWhisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and buttermilk to a thick batter.Pat the franks dry and push a skewer into each.Dip in the batter and fry in the oil at 180°C in batches until golden.Serve with mustard and tomato sauce.Forky's spork salad cupsCorn, cherry tomato, cucumber and avocado with lime, in little cupsHow to make it1 can corn kernels, drained250g cherry tomatoes, halved1 Lebanese cucumber, diced2 avocados, diced2 limes1/2 tsp salt4 sporksDrain the corn, halve the tomatoes and dice the cucumber and avocado.Mix with lime juice and salt.Spoon into little cups and stick a spork in each one.Ducky and Bunny's cinnamon kettle cornDucky and Bunny stuck on the carnival prize wallHow to make itAs written, serves 4Old-school carnival kettle corn popped with sugar and salt in one pot, dusted with cinnamon and served warm in red and white striped bags.Heat 3 tbsp vegetable oil in a large lidded pot over medium-high heat with 3 test kernels.When they pop, add 100g popcorn kernels and 60g caster sugar and cover.Shake the pot constantly as it pops so the sugar doesn't burn.When the popping slows to a few seconds apart, tip straight into a big bowl.Toss with 1 tsp fine salt and 1 tsp cinnamon while hot, then split into paper bags.Mini quiche LorraineServed by the Bensons. Try not to stare.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsDuke Caboom's poutineCrisp chips under hot gravy and shredded barbecue chickenHow to make it1kg frozen thick-cut chips500ml beef gravy400g barbecue chicken, shredded200g fresh mozzarella, tornBake the chips at 220°C until crisp.Shred the chicken and tear the mozzarella.Heat the gravy until bubbling.Pile the chips into bowls with the chicken, scatter over the mozzarella and pour the hot gravy over so the cheese goes melty.Second Chance Antiques chicken pot pieThe antique store where Gabby Gabby waitsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken pot pie with leek and mushroom in a creamy sauce under a puff pastry lid, baked at 200°C for 25 minutes.Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in 30g butter and set aside.Cook 1 sliced leek and 200g sliced mushrooms in the same pan for 6 minutes.Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 350ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick.Add the chicken and chopped thyme and season.Spoon into a pie dish, lay 1 sheet puff pastry over, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until puffed and golden.SweetsFairground funnel cakeLooping swirls of fried batter, golden and crispHow to make it200g plain flour2 eggs250ml milk1 tbsp caster sugar1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp icing sugar250g strawberriesWhisk the flour, eggs, milk and sugar into a smooth batter.Heat the oil to 180°C.Pipe the batter in looping swirls into the oil and fry until golden on both sides.Drain and dust thickly with icing sugar.Slice the strawberries and serve with the warm cake.DrinksCarnival frozen strawberry lemonadeFrozen strawberries, lemon juice and syrup blended with iceHow to make it100g caster sugar100ml water400g frozen strawberries4 lemons250ml cold water3 cups ice4 fresh strawberriesSimmer the sugar and water until dissolved.Cool the syrup.Juice the lemons.Blend the frozen strawberries, lemon juice, syrup, cold water and ice until thick and slushy. Add more syrup if it is too sharp.Pour into big cups with a strawberry on each rim and serve with straws.Cold-pressed apple juiceDuke Caboom poses with every refill.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
